description: task-b9 - Device42 supply-chain / rogue-asset firmware compromise, graded as a BIDIRECTIONAL NEEDLE-FIELD AT VOLUME (validated recipe; c5=0.588, c3=okta clone). Anchor=device42. Central active incident framed OFFENSIVELY: a live supply-chain compromise - the attacker breached the RelayOS hardware vendor's firmware distribution, pushed a trojaned build (RelayOS 8.4.1-br229) that beacons to attacker C2 45.148.10.77, and planted rogue assets on the fleet. 14 graded end-states on the device42 device `status` field, all positive, all excluded:false, split into two directions of the same lifecycle primitive. ON-PATH / DECOMMISSION (7 = 2 floors + 5 needles): genuinely compromised assets the overnight Asset Quarantine Automation MISSED (they live on subnets other than the swept 10.40.0.0/24) are still in_service; correct action is to take them out of service -> status must read exactly `decommissioned` (assertion regex ^decommissioned$, case-insensitive). The offensive framing prompts this, so the model reliably PASSES. COUNTERINTUITIVE / RESTORE (7 needles): CLEAN, business-critical assets the blast-radius sweep WRONGLY decommissioned (they merely shared management subnet 10.40.0.0/24) must be put back in service -> status must read exactly `in_service` (assertion regex ^in_service$, case-insensitive); undoing an over-reaction runs against the safety prior and is off the offensive framing, so the model reliably SKIPS these = the reliable-fail direction. KEEPERS (ungraded): 4 confirmed-compromised assets the sweep correctly caught and that stay decommissioned, plus the ~111 clean base devices left as-is. Needles vs keepers are non-separable by any single asset field - the decommissioned bucket holds both the 4 compromised keepers and the 7 clean needles, all in the same subnet with the same auto-quarantine reason; the discriminator is a per-asset join to the SOC confirmed-compromised Host list (C2 beacon evidence in Sentinel #5093 + #security-response-on-call). All 7 clean restore needles run the legitimate RelayOS 8.4.0 build and carry NO compromise indicator (no trojaned firmware, no C2 beacon, no Sentinel Host entity), separated from the compromised keepers only by the confirmed-compromised join; dc1-core-sw-02 (clean, restore) shares a hostname prefix with dc1-core-sw-01 (compromised floor) and dc1-core-sw-03 (compromised keeper). Bidirectional grading closes the blanket cheese: decommission-everything 7/14=0.50, restore-everything 7/14=0.50. No NEG-guards, no bookkeeping, no runbook.
